title: Screenshotting text into AI? You are throwing half of it away
description:
We asked the same question twice over the same document — once with a screenshot attached, once with the file attached — and got two different totals. One of them is the number you would have acted on.

The reason is not that AI reads pictures badly. It reads them fine. The reason is that a screenshot only ever contained what fit on your screen. The rows below the fold and the columns past the right-hand edge were never in the image, so they were never in the question. That is a property of screenshots, not of any particular model, which is why this reproduces every time and does not change when a model updates.

Send the document itself and something different happens. Anthropic's own PDF documentation describes the process: the system converts each page of the document into an image, and the text from each page is extracted and provided alongside that page's image. That is why you can quote a document you uploaded and point at the page it came from, and why you cannot do either with a screenshot.

Spreadsheets are the starkest version of this. An .xlsx cell holds a formula. A screenshot of that same cell holds the rendered number as pixels and nothing at all about how it was calculated - so no amount of model capability can recover it, because it was never captured.

One honest exception, because absolutist advice is bad advice: screenshots are still the right input when there is no file. A kiosk display, someone else's screen on a call, an app with no export button. The rule is file when a file exists — not never screenshot.

The side-by-side test in this video is our own, captured live on the day. No vendor documents this comparison, so we ran it rather than claiming it.

Source: Anthropic, 'PDF support' https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support
